chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

When you perform the ritual bath after the emergence of dawn, that bathing of yours suffices for the major impurity (janabah), Friday prayer, Arafat, sacrifice, shaving (the head), slaughtering, and pilgrimage; and whenever multiple obligations gather upon you, one bath suffices for them all.
He said, then he said: And similarly for the woman, one bath suffices her for her major impurity, her ihram (state of consecration), Friday prayer, and her bath from menstruation and Eid.
ai.seo_question: Does one ritual bath suffice for multiple obligations like Friday prayer and major impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'jam' al-huquq' (consolidating obligations), where a single ghusl performed after dawn suffices for multiple concurrent ritual impurities and acts of worship, such as Friday prayer, Hajj rites, and Eid. It highlights the practical ease (taysir) in Shia jurisprudence by applying this consolidation equally to women, covering menstruation, ihram, and Eid prayers, thereby reducing the burden of repeated ablutions when duties overlap.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara,

Heasws: ‘When you wash after the emergence of the dawn, that washing of yours would suffice for the sexual impurity, and the Friday, and Arafaat, and the shaving (of the head), and the sacrifice, and the Ziyarat; and whenever the rights gather upon you, one washing would suffice you from these’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And similar to that is the woman, one washing would suffice her for her sexual impurity, and her Friday, and the washing from her menstruation, and her Eid’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “He (the Imam) has said, ‘

If you take a Ghusl (bath) after dawn, it is sufficient for Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relations, for Friday, the day of ‘Arafah, (ninth of Dhul Hajjah), tenth of Dhul Hajjah, for shaving (during Hajj), offering sacrifice and visiting the House (al-Ka‘bah). One Ghusl (bath) suffices many reasons for it.’

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) then said, ‘So also is the case with women. One Ghusl (bath) suffices for sexual relation, assuming the state of ‘Ihram, Friday, Hayd (menses) and for her ‘Id.’”
